explanation: Each ozone molecule has three oxygen atoms instead of the usual two. The 1987 Montreal Protocol led to the phasing out of the CFC gases that were thinning the layer.

claims.text: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs much of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
Carbon dioxide, methane and nitrogen do not form the high layer that blocks the Sun's ultraviolet light.
An ozone molecule has three oxygen atoms, while an ordinary oxygen molecule has two.
The Montreal Protocol, agreed in 1987, led to the phasing out of CFCs.
CFCs released by people were thinning the ozone layer.
